title: Configuring Tree Discovery in Zscaler and Deploying to AWS

blocks.text: The first step in Onboarding an AWS Organization, is to configure and deploy a Tree Discovery template that allows Zscaler to discover all the organizational units (OUs) and accounts in your AWS Organization.
To configure and deploy a Tree Discovery template, do the following:

blocks.item: 1. Define the discovery scope and settings in Zscaler.
To define the discovery scope and settings in Zscaler, do the following:
In the AI Security Admin Portal, go to Administration > Account Onboarding.
Click + Add New.
In the Start Onboarding window, select Cloud Providers.
In the Select Cloud Provider window, select the AWS tile and click Next.
In the Select Deployment Mode section, select Zscaler Hosted (Recommended) and click Next.
See image.
In the Select Onboarding Type window, select AWS Organization and click Next.
In the Configuration Creation Mode, select Automated Role Creation (Recommended) and click Next.
Select Manual Role Creation if your environment requires your team to create the IAM roles and policies manually.
See image.
In the Tree Discovery section, enter the following details from your AWS Management Account:
Integration Alias: Enter a user-friendly name for the AWS Organization.
Organization ID: Enter the AWS Organization ID, for example, o-abc1234567
External ID: Enter any alphanumeric value between 2 and 1224 characcters.
Management Account ID: Enter the AWS Account ID of the organization’s root or management account
Tree Discovery Role Name: Enter the name of the IAM role Zscaler creates in the management account.

Email IDs (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded tenant. You can add up to 30 email addresses to receive notifications about the issues. You can also add email addresses after completing the onboarding process.
Click Save Integration. The next steps vary depending on the type of role creation you choose during Configuration Creation Mode.
For Automated Role Creation
A prompt appears to download the Tree Discovery template.
See image.
In the Deploy Tree Discovery section, select one of the following:
Download Template: To download the CloudFormation (CFT) or Terraform template to your local machine.
Quick Deploy: You are redirected to the AWS Portal. Ensure you have logged into the correct Management Account.
Copy the External ID that is generated in the AI Security console.
See image.
Paste the copied text into the External ID field in the AWS Portal, under CloudFormation > Stacks > Quick create stack.
See image.
Click Save.
For Manual Role Creation

Before creating the Tree Discovery IAM role in AWS, you need the exact trust policy and permissions policy JSON provided by the AI Security Console that define what the role trusts (the AssumeRolePolicyDocument) and what it is permitted to do (both the managed and inline permissions policies). In the Tree Discovery Role Reference section, do the following:

Click Copy next to the Trust Policy (AssumeRolePolicyDocument) to copy its JSON text, then paste it into the corresponding field in the AWS Console. To learn more, see Creating IAM Roles for Tree Discovery.
Click Copy next to the Permissions Policy (managed) to copy the JSON text, then paste it into the corresponding field in the AWS Console. To learn more, see Creating IAM Roles for Tree Discovery.
Click Copy next to the Permissions Policy (inline) to copy the JSON text, then paste it into the corresponding field in the AWS Console. To learn more, see Creating IAM Roles for Tree Discovery.
Click Next.
2. Deploy the generated template to the target AWS accounts (for automated role creation).
To deploy the tree discovery template, do the following:
Deploy the CloudFormation template in AWS.
Sign in to the AWS Management Console and go to CloudFormation.
In the left-side navigation, select Stacks.
Click Create stack.
On the Create stack page:
Prepare template: Select Template is ready.
Specify template: Select Upload a template file to upload the template you downloaded from the AI Security Admin Portal
Upload a template file: Click Choose file, browse and select template, then click Open.
Click Next.
On the Specify stack details page, under Stack name, enter a unique stack name.
Click Next.
On the Configure stack options page, click Next.
On the Review and create page, under Capabilities, select the I acknowledge checkbox to acknowledge AWS CloudFormation's creation of IAM resources with custom names.
Click Submit.
Deploy the Terraform template in AWS.
Update the backend.tf file with the name of the storage services where you want to store the Terraform state files. For example:
bucket: Enter the name of the S3 bucket.
region: Enter the region.
dynamodb_table: Enter the name of the dynamoDB table.
Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
Switch to the directory that contains the Terraform template.
Copy and paste the access keys of the target account and press Enter.
Run the following commands:
To initialize the Terraform working directory:
terraform init
To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration:
terraform plan
To run the Terraform script:
terraform apply
For Do you want to perform these actions?, enter yes and press Enter.
AI Security validates the template deployment every hour by checking the IAM roles and permissions.
3. Confirm the deployed accounts appear and are discovered in Zscaler.
To discover accounts in Zscaler, do the following:
Return to the AI Security console, and in the Discover Member Accounts section, click Discover Accounts.
Zscaler uses the cross-account role deployed in the previous step to discover all AWS accounts in the organization. The total number of discovered accounts is displayed.
Click Next.

blocks.text: After configuring and deploying the tree template and discovering accounts, you are directed to Complete the Configuration in Zscaler.
